paragraphs.title: A Call to Song and Shofar Blowing

easy.explanation: The title identifies the psalm as being to Asaph.
easy.q: To whom is the psalm attributed?

easy.explanation: The passage calls for a psalm, a joyful noise, and musical instruments.
easy.q: How are the people called to praise God?

easy.explanation: Verse 3 says, “Blow up the trumpet in the new moon.”
easy.q: What instrument were the people told to blow?

answers: Singing, playing instruments, and blowing the trumpet
Leaving Egypt, then singing and praying
Warning against idols, then playing instruments
medium.explanation: The passage moves from singing to instruments and then to the trumpet.
medium.q: What sequence appears in these verses?

medium.explanation: The trumpet was to be blown “in the time appointed, on our solemn feast day.”
medium.q: When was the trumpet blowing especially appointed?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a designated day of solemn celebration.
medium.q: What does “our solemn feast day” refer to?

answers: They are different ways of praising God
challenge.explanation: The verses present several forms of joyful worship together.
challenge.q: What do the song, instruments, and trumpet have in common?

challenge.explanation: The passage calls them “a statute for Israel” and “a law of the God of Jacob.”
challenge.q: How are these worship practices described for Israel?

answers: It is connected with the new moon and feast day
It is connected only with farming
It is connected only with Joseph
challenge.explanation: The trumpet is associated with the new moon and the appointed feast.
challenge.q: What connection is made between the trumpet and time?

paragraphs.title: God’s Kindness to Joseph and Israel

easy.explanation: Verse 5 refers to Joseph and his experience in Egypt.
easy.q: Whose experience is recalled in these verses?

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I removed his shoulder from the burden.”

answers: He sent them back to Egypt
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “Thou calledst in trouble, and I delivered thee.”
easy.q: What did God do when His people were in trouble?

answers: Joseph’s hardship and deliverance, followed by Israel’s deliverance
Israel’s warning against idols, followed by Joseph’s birth
A harvest of wheat, followed by trumpet blowing
medium.explanation: The passage recalls Joseph’s burden and then God’s answer to Israel in trouble.
medium.q: What is the main sequence in this passage?

answers: I sent you to a feast
medium.explanation: The expression means that God rescued the person who called to Him.
medium.q: What does “I delivered thee” mean in context?

answers: Testing at the waters of Meribah
medium.explanation: The Lord says, “I proved thee at the waters of Meribah.”
medium.q: What event is mentioned along with God’s answer?

challenge.explanation: Both Joseph and Israel are described in connection with deliverance from hardship.
challenge.q: What common idea links Joseph’s experience and Israel’s experience?

answers: To remember God’s former acts of mercy
challenge.explanation: The passage remembers how God heard and rescued His people.
challenge.q: Why are these past events recalled?

answers: When people call, God delivers and answers
Trouble causes people to stop listening
People in trouble must rely only on instruments
challenge.explanation: The Lord says, “Thou calledst in trouble, and I delivered thee.”
challenge.q: What relationship is shown between trouble and God’s response?

easy.explanation: God says, “Hear, O my people,” and calls Israel to hearken unto Him.
easy.q: What does God ask His people to do?

easy.explanation: The Lord forbids any strange god and the worship of any strange god.
easy.q: What were the people forbidden to worship?

easy.explanation: God identifies Himself as the One who brought Israel out of Egypt.
easy.q: Who brought Israel out of Egypt?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “My people would not hearken to my voice.”
medium.q: How did the people respond to God’s voice?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that Israel followed its own advice instead of God’s ways.
medium.q: What does “Israel had walked in their own counsels” mean?

answers: He gave them up to their own desires
He sent them back to Egypt
He stopped reminding them of the Exodus
medium.explanation: The Lord says, “So I gave them up unto their own hearts’ lust.”
medium.q: What did God do after the people refused to listen?

answers: To show why they should listen to Him
To encourage worship of strange gods
To explain the use of musical instruments
challenge.explanation: The reminder identifies God as their deliverer and supports His call for obedience.
challenge.q: Why does God remind Israel that He brought them out of Egypt?

answers: Refusal to hear and obey God
Blowing the trumpet at a feast
challenge.explanation: Israel would not hearken, so it followed its own desires and counsel.
challenge.q: What led Israel to walk in its own counsels?

answers: God’s call to listen versus Israel’s refusal
challenge.explanation: God calls His people to hearken, but the people refuse His voice.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in the passage?

paragraphs.title: The Promise of Protection and Abundance

easy.explanation: The psalmist says, “Oh that my people had hearkened unto me.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist wish Israel would do?

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I should soon have subdued their enemies.”
easy.q: What would God do to Israel’s enemies?

answers: The finest of the wheat and honey
easy.explanation: The final verse speaks of the finest wheat and honey out of the rock.
easy.q: What food is promised to God’s people?

medium.explanation: The promise follows the wish that Israel would listen and walk in God’s ways.
medium.q: What condition is connected with the promise of protection?

medium.explanation: To subdue enemies is to defeat or bring them under control.
medium.q: What does “subdued” mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: God promises the finest wheat and honey out of the rock.
medium.q: What is promised after the enemies are subdued?

answers: Listening to God is connected with protection and abundance
challenge.explanation: The passage connects hearkening to God with subdued enemies and rich provision.

answers: They submit to Him, while their time endures forever
They are brought out of Egypt
challenge.explanation: The verse says the haters of the LORD should have submitted, but their time should have endured forever.
challenge.q: What is said about those who hate the LORD?

answers: God’s people receive provision, while His haters face judgment
Both receive the same food and blessing
God’s people face punishment, while His haters receive abundance
challenge.explanation: Israel is promised wheat and honey, while the haters of the LORD are described as remaining under judgment.
challenge.q: What contrast is made between God’s people and His haters?
